svg.title: Bench wiring: Orange Pi 4 Pro + PZ7020 FPGA + Teensy 4.1
svg.text: Orange Pi 4 Pro + PZ7020 FPGA board + Teensy 4.1
Every cable and every wire. Nothing else connects: NOT the Pi's GPIO pins,
NOT the FPGA's JM2 header, NOT the FPGA's lower Ethernet jack.
SD card in the underside slot
Orange Pi Ethernet port → FPGA UPPER Ethernet jack (ETH-PS).
Normal Ethernet cable. Pi = 10.77.0.1, FPGA = 10.77.0.2. Carries the GPU, matrix engine, RAM swap.
Orange Pi USB-A port → Teensy micro-USB.
A USB DATA cable, not charge-only. It powers the Teensy.
Teensy pins → FPGA header JM1: 22 jumper wires.
Wire with BOTH boards unpowered, grounds first. Power DOWN: unplug the Teensy's USB FIRST, then J8.
5 V USB-A charger, 2 A or more → FPGA UPPER USB-C (J8).
Use a USB-A → USB-C cable. A C-to-C cable gives this board NO power.
FPGA LOWER USB-C (J2) → this PC. Optional.
Lets watch_boot.ps1 record the FPGA's boot report.
FPGA HDMI → a monitor or TV.
The GPU's screen: colour bars, then dark blue when it is running.
Also: the Pi's own power supply; the NVMe in the Pi's M.2 slot; an optional fan on JM1 1 (5 V), 3 (GND),
B. The 22 jumper wires: FPGA JM1 ↔ Teensy
Both boards drawn as they sit on the bench, top side up.
Each wire has a number (W1–W22) marked on its pin on BOTH boards. Fit W1–W3 (grounds) first.
FPGA board, TOP EDGE — header JM1
□ Square pad = pin 1, at the left end of the inner row. Odd pins: inner row. Even pins: outer row.
Never a Teensy wire on 1 (5 V), 2 (3.3 V), 3, 5, 7 (the fan). Pin 4 IS a ground wire (W1). 35 and 36 stay empty.
Teensy 4.1 — top side up, USB at the LEFT
The Vin edge, from the USB end: Vin, GND, 3.3V, 23 … 13, GND, 41 … 33.
The pin 0 edge, from the USB end: GND, 0 … 12, 3.3V, 24 … 32. Vin and 3.3V (red): NEVER wired.
Checked when this was drawn: the Teensy firmware, the FPGA pin file, the vendor's JM1 table
and WIRING.md agree on every wire. Every pin carries at most one wire. No wire touches 5 V,
3.3 V or the fan's pins. Both boards are 3.3 V logic: wires go direct, no resistors.
